text:
maria: FYI seeing weird p95 delta across regions for same A100 SKU + same driver family. AWS is ~300ms, GCP ~420ms, Azure ~440ms for gpt-small-v1, bs=1, seq=1024, int8 quant run. Plot: https://perf.redwood/internal/runs/1729981119 :eyes:
lee: can you paste the exact driver/CUDA and the command you used?
maria: quick dump: 
```
# AWS
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,cuda_version,name --format=csv
525.60,12.1,A100-PCIE-40GB
# GCP
525.85,12.1,A100-PCIE-40GB
# Azure
525.85,12.1,A100-PCIE-40GB
```
maria: runtime args: `--batch-size 1 --max-seq 1024 --quant int8 --kernel fused-gemm-v2`
sanjay: hmmm same CUDA, minor driver dot diff. Have we ruled out NUMA and I/O? GCP images default to `autosetting numa` sometimes. Try `numactl --physcpubind=+0-47 --membind=0`
anya: infra telemetry shows GCP instances were on host with heavy colocated memcpy jobs during that window (network backups). I can re-run on a clean host.
lee: also check cublasLt and tuned kernel selection — our kernel selector picks different tiling for certain sm versions when driver >=525.80. Could explain extra copy/transpose.
maria: re-ran on fresh GCP host (no colocation), new numbers: p50/p95: 120ms / 360ms. AWS still 300ms. Azure 430ms. so GCP improved but still worse.
sanjay: do you have perf counters? cache-miss, l2, dram bw?
maria: attached perf-bot summary: 
```
perf-bot: summary run 1729981130
- AWS: p95 298ms, L2 hit 72%, DRAM bw 680GB/s
- GCP: p95 362ms, L2 hit 61%, DRAM bw 710GB/s
- Azure: p95 432ms, L2 hit 58%, DRAM bw 705GB/s
notes: GCP/Azure show higher global memory stalls and lower L2 locality for our int8 kernels.
```
lee: lower L2 hit for same SKU suggests either microcode/firmware or topology differences (NUMA placement of GPU BAR or host CPU affinity). Also check kernel driver microcode (GPU BIOS) versions.
anya: I can get host BIOS and firmware for the three runs. I'll also schedule a deterministic run on pinned cores + `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=0` to remove scheduling noise.
maria: one more datapoint: changing kernel to `baseline-gemm` (no fused transpose) makes GCP ~305ms, Azure ~310ms, AWS 320ms. So fused path seems to be the trouble on GCP/Azure.
sanjay: that points to a kernel selection/codepath difference in our fused-gemm-v2 that triggers on driver microversion >=525.80. Maybe a codepath uses an unoptimized tile size for certain SM/PCIe pacing.
lee: action items: (1) anya to fetch host firmware/BIOS/VM kernel flags (2) perf-bot to run fused vs baseline config sweep across all regions at bs=1,seq=512/1024 (3) maria to open a model-onboard eval with these perf traces attached and mark quant regression tag.
anya: will do, scheduled runs in 30m. cc @lee @sanjay :thumbsup:
perf-bot: queued sweep job 1729981167. results will post to the thread when done.
maria: thanks — if sweep shows fused path regression we should consider pinning kernel selector to baseline for customers on 525.80+ until we fix.
lee: agreed. quick mitigation: override `REDWOOD_KERNEL_SELECTOR=force-baseline` per-deployment.
maria: noted. I'll file a short rollback runbook if perf-bot confirms. :memo:
